simple.meaning: רָחֵל (râchêl) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a ewe [the females being the predominant element of a flock] (as a good traveller ).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 31:38. The surrounding context includes flock.

simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.short: a ewe [the females being the predominant element of a flock] (as a good traveller )
definitions.full: H7353. rachel I. רָחֵל noun feminine Isa 53:7 ewe ; — absolute ׳ר 53:7 (in simile, || שֶׂה ); plural רְחֵלִים Gen 32:15 (E; + אֵילִים עִזִּים, ), Song 6:6 (in simile); suffix וְעִזֶּיךָ רְחֵלֶיךָ Gen 31:38 (E).
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to journey ;

occurrences.englishText: “These twenty years I have been with you. Your ewes and your female goats have not cast their young, and I haven’t eaten the rams of your flocks.
thirty milk camels and their colts, forty cows, ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten foals.
